summary: Mervin Viggo Hanson specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia (attested 1980), studying under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz and teacher Kathryn A. A. Cissell.
Mettanando Bhikkhu is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under the doctoral supervision of Barend Jan Terwiel.

Michael Alram is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1975–1982), where he held a post in ~1987, and worked at the Kunsthistorisches Museum (~1986–2021).

Michael Aris was a Tibetology and history/archaeology scholar. Educated at Durham and London under David L. Snellgrove, he held posts at St John's College, Wolfson College, St Antony's College, the University of Oxford (~1980–1999), and Harvard (~1992–1993).
Michael Balk specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1988 and held a post at the Berlin State Library (attested 1991).

Michael Baxandall studied at Downing College (~1951–1954). He held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum (1961–1965), the Warburg Institute (~1965–1986), Cornell University (~1982–1987), and the University of California, Berkeley (~1987–1996).

Michael Carrithers is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held a post at Wolfson College, Oxford, in 1977 and served as Lecturer in Social Anthropology at Durham University (~1982–1993).
Michael Chase is a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Victoria and the École Pratique des Hautes Études. In ~2001, he held a post as a researcher in ancient philosophy at the CNRS.

Michael Comans specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and Jan Willem de Jong at the Australian National University (~1983–1987), later holding a post at the University of Sydney (~1989–1999).

Michael Como specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Bernard Faure, Carl Bielefeldt, and Kuo-liang Wang, and held a post at Columbia University (attested 2009).

Michael D. Willis is an Indology, history, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Victoria and Chicago. He held posts at UBC, SUNY New Paltz, De Montfort, the British Museum (1994–2003, 2005–2014), and the European Research Council (2014–2020).
Michael Friedrich is a sinology and Buddhist studies scholar who succeeded Friedrich Alexander Bischoff. He was appointed Professor at the University of Hamburg in ~1994.
Michael G. Morony is a history, archaeology, and religious studies scholar. He studied at UC Berkeley and UCLA (~1962–1971), where he later served as Professor beginning in ~1974.

Michael Hahn was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and Tibetologist. Educated at Göttingen, Bonn, and Marburg under Wilhelm Rau and Franz Bernhard, he held posts at Bonn, the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (~1988–2002), and the University of Marburg (~1992–2007).
Michael Hookham is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who founded the Longchen Foundation. He studied under traditional teachers Chögyam Trungpa (1965) and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Michael Hutt specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of London and SOAS (~1976–1984), where he became Lecturer in Nepali in ~1987.

Michael J. Sweet was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, later serving there as clinical assistant professor in the Department of Psychiatry (attested 1996, 2006).
Michael J. Tetreault is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He earned his Master of Arts at San Diego State University under supervisor Sandra A. Wawrytko (attested 2011).

Michael J. Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of Cape Town (~1986–1989), the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1991–1994), and completed doctoral studies under William F. Powell (~1994–2000).

Michael K. Jerryson was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Harold Scheub. He held religious studies posts at Eckerd College (~2008–2012) and Youngstown State University (~2012–2021).
